Travel paperwork weekly rules

Purpose: keep pet travel files complete, readable, and ready for review so customers get steady help and animals move with clear care notes.

The Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways checks each file for the right travel papers, the booking match, and any care notes that affect handling. Staff keep the tone calm and practical, because owners often arrive worried and need plain answers. When a passenger shares a concern, the desk listens fully, records the point in clear language, and passes it to the cabin team or supervisor without delay. If the animal has special needs, the file should show species, temperament, feeding needs, crate condition, and any comfort steps that reduce stress. Staff should avoid guessing and should update the record only after confirming the facts with the passenger or the source document.

Paperwork is to be checked as a routine part of the weekly workflow, with attention to missing signatures, unclear contact details, and any mismatch between the ticket and the pet record. If a detail is unclear, the desk asks for correction before approval rather than letting a weak file move forward. Good records help the cabin team monitor animals during flight and give the crew a fair chance to respond to changes in behavior, noise, or comfort. The desk should also note any handoff instructions so that the supervisor can follow the same care plan from check-in to arrival.

When more than one pet is linked to a booking, staff must keep each animal's notes separate and easy to trace. A clean file protects the customer and helps prevent mixed instructions, missed alerts, or unnecessary stress for the animal. The team should use simple wording, short entries, and a steady review habit so that work stays consistent across shifts. If a case needs extra judgment, the desk should escalate it rather than settle it informally.

For questions about a file, service concern, or exception, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor.
